checkpoint_finding.rule: A future state is target-label-unexposed only when expression preprocessing, graph construction, autoencoder fit, reconstruction choices, clustering, and label mapping are restricted to the registered participant split.

input_eligibility.gse192741: Visium expression and coordinates are structurally compatible, but four donors and unresolved hg19 annotation permit only technical fixtures.
input_eligibility.gse292268: CosMx expression and coordinates are structurally compatible as a separate single-cell panel stratum, but donor joins are unresolved and four donors are underpowered.
input_eligibility.hra007511: Visium RNA could be used only after permission, participant and section joins, rights, and runtime admission. H&E and MALDI are not inputs.
input_eligibility.vu2025: Visium RNA could be used only after the DSA and participant map clear. Graphs may not span participants sharing a VLP array.

exposure_and_leakage_findings.native_fit: STAGATE trains a graph-attention autoencoder on the supplied target expression and graph and commonly clusters its target embedding. This is transductive.
exposure_and_leakage_findings.preprocessing: Normalization, log transform, HVGs, feature order, scaling, graph radius or K, architecture, epochs, and clustering must stay inside development participants unless a transductive task explicitly permits target fitting.
exposure_and_leakage_findings.graph: Two-dimensional graphs must be participant- and section-blocked. A technical array or shared coordinate range cannot define biological adjacency.
exposure_and_leakage_findings.three_dimensional: The source can add cross-section edges using section order and distance. This is prohibited absent same-participant sections, authoritative registration and physical spacing, and a precommitted 3D objective.
exposure_and_leakage_findings.reconstruction: Mean-squared reconstructed normalized expression is model-derived continuous output, not observed counts or additional biological replicates.

known_incidents_and_biases: The selected PyTorch Geometric implementation states that the published cell-type-aware module is unsupported.
The PyG converter densifies the expression matrix and can exceed memory on high-resolution sections.
The source sets cudnn deterministic and benchmark flags together, so deterministic behavior is not established.
The official workflow has no pretrained checkpoint, complete model export, or native frozen held-donor predictor.
The Zenodo publication archive is the TensorFlow reference implementation rather than the selected PyG source.
Target-fitted reconstruction and clustering can improve in-sample structure without demonstrating participant-held transfer.
remaining_blockers: Obtain a rights-cleared powered participant-linked spatial RNA dataset, registered endpoint, transcript-native baselines, and external source.
Implement separate native-transductive and benchmark-defined strict lanes with participant-blocked graphs and training-only preprocessing and clustering choices.
Keep the 3D graph path disabled unless authoritative same-participant section topology, registration, physical spacing, and a precommitted objective pass admission.
Replace the dense expression conversion with a memory-safe path and demonstrate fixed-fixture parity.
Resolve an exact runtime, deterministic policy, and safe tensor-only state export that binds feature and graph order.

After activation and campaign approval, pass SLURM import, sparse-memory, graph-boundary, 3D prohibition, forward, backward, resume, deterministic seed, node-order, section-order, no-network, and cross-device fixtures.
interpretation: STAGATE is a future target-fitted graph autoencoder baseline. It has no pretrained-corpus contamination, but local split, graph, preprocessing, reconstruction, clustering, memory, and determinism risks remain. No eligible spatial task or external source exists, so it remains deferred.
